/-!
# Convergence of the Flint Hills and Cookson Hills series

*References:*
- [Wikipedia: Examples of numerical series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Series_(mathematics)#Examples_of_numerical_series)
- [MathWorld: Flint Hills Series](https://mathworld.wolfram.com/FlintHillsSeries.html)
- [Alekseyev, On the Flint Hills series](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.1104.5100)
- [MathWorld: Cookson Hills Series](https://mathworld.wolfram.com/CooksonHillsSeries.html)
-/

namespace FlintCooksonHills

/--
The Flint Hills series summing $csc(n)^2 / n^3$ from $n=1$ to $\infty$ converges.
(Note that we 0-index the series below.)
-/
@[category research open, AMS 40]
theorem flint_hills_series_converges :
    answer(sorry) ↔
      Summable (fun n : ℕ =>
        1 / ((((n + 1) : ℝ)^3) * (Real.sin (n + 1)^2))) := by
  sorry

/--
The Cookson Hills series summing $sec(n)^2 / n^3$ from $n=1$ to $\infty$ converges.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 40]
theorem cookson_hills_series_converges :
    answer(sorry) ↔
      Summable (fun n : ℕ =>
        1 / ((((n + 1) : ℝ)^3) * (Real.cos (n + 1)^2))) := by
  sorry

end FlintCooksonHills

reformulations.difference: Lean uses unconditional Summable over ℕ with the shifted reciprocal summand, whereas the source asks about ordinary convergence of ∑_{n=1}∞ csc²(n)/n³.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The summands are nonnegative, so Mathlib's hasSum_iff_tendsto_nat_of_nonneg identifies unconditional summability with convergence of ordinary partial sums to a real number. The substitution n ↦ n+1 takes the sum over range N exactly to the sum over Icc 1 N, and 1/(n³ sin²(n)) = (1/sin(n))²/n³. The complete equivalence is proved as Review.flint_equiv_source in /workspace/review/scratch.lean, without sorryAx dependencies.

reformulations.difference: Lean uses unconditional Summable over ℕ with the shifted reciprocal summand, whereas the source asks about ordinary convergence of ∑_{n=1}∞ sec²(n)/n³.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: All summands are nonnegative, making unconditional summability equivalent to ordinary partial-sum convergence by hasSum_iff_tendsto_nat_of_nonneg. Reindexing by n ↦ n+1 gives exactly the positive-integer series, and 1/(n³ cos²(n)) = (1/cos(n))²/n³. The complete equivalence is proved as Review.cookson_equiv_source in /workspace/review/scratch.lean, without sorryAx dependencies.

review.notes: Both answer placeholders have the correct top-level Prop scope and yes/no polarity. Lean checks establish the correct first terms and strict positivity of both denominators at every actual index, so division-by-zero defaults do not affect either problem. The scratch file compiles successfully. Both MathWorld articles still explicitly state that convergence is unknown. Although their linked arXiv:2502.03474 claims convergence, the inspected argument incorrectly asserts Hölder continuity of the floor function; I did not treat this preprint as an accepted resolution or recommend changing the open tags.
